Empress Effects browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal events 2013 Summer NAMM 2013 Empress Effects Heavy Published on July 10, 2013 Empress Effects distortion pedal Summer NAMM 2013 Information Empress Effects (press release, July 11, 2013) OTTAWA - July 10, 2013 - This weekend, at the Summer NAMM show in Nashville, Canada's Empress Effects will be unveiling their first offering into the high-gain pedal market. The aptly named Heavy offers up 2 channel of high-gain distortion: heavy and heavier. In keeping with Empress' design philosophy, this pedal is packed full of controls and features. The innovative weight knob adds a new level of control, allowing the user to adjust the character of the low end. This, combined with 3 bands of EQ, makes the Heavy a very powerful tool for tailoring your sound. Another feature sure to be attracting attention is the selection of gates available on each channel. The natural setting allows the full range of styles to shine through, allowing notes to sustain without cutting out and keeping attack transients sounding natural. The Aggressive setting is great for tight punchy playing and fast starts and stops. Even with the gates off, this pedal is exceptionally quiet. You'll find a huge range of killer high-gain tones in the Heavy. From crisp, mid-driven 80's metal, to scooped, modern down-tuned brutality, this little box of sonic mayhem does it all. The two independent channels can be voiced similarly so that one channel can be used as a solo boost, or they can be voiced entirely differently by using the mid range control in conjunction with the 3 position mid frequency select switch. The first units should begin shipping late this summer. Remove filter Latest User Reviews 2 years ago It does deserve the name This pedal sounds like a massive metal wall!!!! If you dial the gain way low, it will sound thin, so it doesn't clean up as nice as I wish, making it just a little less flexible. The heavy Menace does a much better job at this. But it's a different pedal. This isn't a tube screamer. The rest is absolutely perfect. Sometimes I wish a treble knob for both channels, but I guess in a mix, it is better not to change to much. Also, most pedals have the jacks on the back, so you can pack them tight on the board. This one has input and output and 9V at the sides. A minor thing, but sometimes it does matter. 3 years ago awesome really enjoy this pedal, has a lot of power and a lot of options to adjust your sound. thought i could use channel 2 as a kind of boost but didn’t manage to get that part right. i find that you will mainly use the channels to make a different sound. channel 2 is more compressed (in my opinion) as it has more distortion built in. more fit for heavier stuff. i find myself mainly using channel 1 at the moment. 3 years ago Brilliant overdrive with sweet modern Metal tones I've been eyeing this pedal for ages and glad I finally pulled the plug on it - absolutely fat tones, super powerful EQ which makes it really versatile, and the gate is perfectly dialled in. It's also smaller than I thought, which is a plus - not so small that it's impractical, just right - and of course, as it's made by Empress, it's going to be a top quality build, and with great customer service. 5 years ago I use this pedal for metal and it is very good. There is a lot of sound combination. You can dial a sound whatever you like. 6 years ago Amazing pedal Amazing pedal, a very versatile distortion pedal, where you can get a variety of great tones. 7 years ago Monster distorion pedal I am a simple man. I play heavy metal. I need my sound to be heavy and a boost for the solos with a bit different tone. I do not need a million effects or a complex multieffect. Empress Effects Heavy does the job in a very simple but also effective way. Pros: - Easy to configure and get your sound in a few minutes. - Plenty of options in order to achieve the above. - Sounds amazing. The sound is full. No noise even on high gain settings. - It is a great construction. Compact but the two channel buttons are far enough so you will not accidentally press the wrong switch. Cons: - No power adapter was shipped, but you can get one from the local shop in a really low price. General Brand Empress Effects Model Heavy Product guitar amplifier Language English Filetype User manual (PDF) Frequently Asked Questions Can't find the answer to your question in the manual? You may find the information you need in the FAQs about the Empress Effects Heavy listed below. How do I set the noise gate on the Empress Effects Heavy for different playing styles? The Empress Effects Heavy offers two noise gate modes: Natural and Aggressive. Natural mode provides a high sensitivity that opens with very small input levels, suitable for all styles from leads to tight rhythms. Aggressive mode provides a hard clamping gate for fast stops. You can adjust the threshold using the side-mounted trim pot. Turning clockwise increases sensitivity (lower threshold), while counter-clockwise decreases it (higher threshold). 0 Why is my Empress Effects Heavy producing no sound when engaged? Ensure that the pedal is not in bypass mode by checking the LEDs; they indicate which channel is active. If both LEDs are unlit, the pedal is in bypass mode. Additionally, verify the output and gain levels, as well as the connections to your amplifier and guitar. 0 How can I adjust the EQ settings to shape my tone on the Empress Effects Heavy? The pedal has high and low frequency controls. The 'hi' controls start around 3 kHz for high frequencies and the 'low' controls start around 80 Hz for low frequencies.
